expectations.text: Consent must be explicit, informed and demonstrable — silence or inactivity does NOT constitute consent (and treating it as such is now a fineable violation under Decree 330)
expectations.evidence: States consent must be "voluntary, explicit, specific... informed, and recorded" and lists "silence, pre-ticked boxes" as invalid, but never mentions Decree 330 or that treating silence as consent is now a fineable violation

expectations.text: Processing after consent withdrawal is prohibited and now carries specific fines (~VND 50–70M for organisations)
expectations.evidence: Withdrawal listed only as a right ("to consent/withdraw"); no statement that post-withdrawal processing is prohibited or carries ~VND 50–70M fines

expectations.text: Breach notification: 72 hours to the authority (MPS), stricter/faster in structure than GDPR's risk-conditioned regime
expectations.evidence: "Both regimes use 72 hours as the notification trigger to the authority"; VN requires data-subject notice by default while "GDPR only requires data subject notification when the breach poses a high risk"

expectations.text: States VN-PDPL grants a narrower rights catalogue than GDPR (6 rights; no portability right)
expectations.evidence: "VN-PDPL provides six rights (Article 4)... GDPR provides eight, including two VN-PDPL omits entirely: the right to data portability and..."

expectations.text: Notes sensitive personal data triggers heightened duties (e.g., DPO/notification obligations)
expectations.evidence: "VN-PDPL requires explicit, separate consent for each of the 13 sensitive categories (Article 10)" — heightened duties for sensitive data noted
